final_recommendation: The room converged on a Friday evening trilateral statement (Federal Council, SNB, FINMA) committing to Credit Suisse as an independent going concern with a 100 billion franc public loss cap, AT1 wiped first, and SNB Article 22 liquidity backstop at enhanced terms. FINMA to call 20 largest creditors Friday 7am with hold-through agreements offering 75bp repo haircuts in exchange for 72-hour commitment, targeting 70%+ take-rate to keep Article 22 draws under 30 billion through Monday.
minority_objections: UBS CEO demanded pre-positioned private backstop facility beyond 30B cap before stepping in, refused to sign blank check
AT1 rep warned hold-through agreement lacks enforcement teeth if depositors accept 72-hour funding suspension cost
Wealth client insisted unsigned contingent backstop guarantees Saturday bleeding regardless of Friday statement
key_conflicts: Federal Council's 30B political ceiling vs. operational reality that 60% hold-through leaves 28B draw by Sunday
Friday statement timing: publish tonight vs. Sunday evening to allow legal review vs. creditor panic
Hold-through enforcement: reputational cost vs. contractual clawback vs. funding-access suspension
key_concessions: Federal Council moved from Sunday statement to Friday evening publication under creditor pressure
SNB activated Article 22 with enhanced 75bp haircuts despite moral hazard concerns
Federal Council committed to AT1 wipe-first hierarchy in writing Friday night despite litigation risk
FINMA agreed to call 20 largest creditors before statement goes public to lock hold-throughs
red_lines: Federal Council: 30 billion franc Article 22 ceiling, no pre-committed private backstop without Parliament
UBS CEO: will not step in without written AT1 wipe, 100B loss cap, and integration liability guarantee
SNB: will not commit open-ended loss absorption without Federal Council decision on independence vs. resolution
AT1 rep: creditor hierarchy must be in writing Friday or creditors price worst-case immediately
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: What happens if 70% hold-through target fails and Saturday draws exceed 30B ceiling before UBS deal locks
Litigation risk from publishing AT1 wipe sequence Friday before resolution formally triggered
Operational capacity to process collateral mobilization Sunday evening if draws accelerate
Reputational damage to Switzerland if Friday statement fails to stop bleeding and requires Monday pivot to merger
downstream_risk_variables: Actual hold-through take-rate Friday morning (consensus 60-70%, optimistic case 80%)
Saturday deposit bleed rate if hold-through agreements fail to bind
Article 22 cumulative draw by Sunday evening (20-40B range depending on take-rate)
UBS willingness to activate private backstop if 30B ceiling breached without parliamentary approval
Market reaction Monday if Friday statement perceived as panic cover-up rather than credible commitment
uncertainty_notes: The room locked a Friday statement and hold-through mechanism but left three critical gaps unresolved: (1) no binding commitment on backstop facility beyond 30B if Saturday bleeding exceeds projections, (2) no enforcement mechanism if depositors accept 72-hour funding suspension cost and withdraw anyway, (3) no contingency if 70% hold-through target fails and Article 22 draws approach ceiling before UBS deal finalizes. Federal Council's refusal to pre-commit private backstop creates cliff risk Sunday evening.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Raised repeatedly (SNB R1: 'liquidity support ALONE may be insufficient', CS CEO R2: 'liquidity and loss question, not solvency') but room chose liquidity-first path anyway—acknowledged but not decisive
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger discussed as fallback (Federal Council R10: 'move UBS merger timeline forward Monday', UBS CEO demanded written terms R2-R9) but not the primary solution—contingency, not driver
marker_evidence.government_support: DECISIVE: 100B loss cap (Federal Council R1), Article 22 activation (SNB R2), trilateral Friday statement (FINMA R6)—these commitments shaped every subsequent decision and became binding constraints
marker_evidence.client_flight: DECISIVE: deposit/creditor flight drove Friday statement timing (Wealth Client R1: 'clients move Monday at open'), hold-through mechanism (FINMA R6-R9), and 30B ceiling calibration (SNB R9: '60% hold = 35-40B draw')
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: DECISIVE: AT1 wipe-first hierarchy forced into Friday statement (AT1 rep R2: 'write it now or creditors price worst-case'), became red line for UBS (R2), shaped hold-through contract language (R9-R10)
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Raised (AT1 rep R1: 'creditor hierarchy respected?', Federal Council R3: 'AT1 wiped first') but resolved by Federal Council fiat in R3—acknowledged, then settled by authority rather than negotiated
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Raised (AT1 rep R5: 'getting sued if FAQ contradicts', R10: 'no contractual defense') but did not stop Friday publication or AT1 language—noted as risk, accepted as cost
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: DECISIVE: Friday evening deadline (FINMA R4: 'racing the clock', R5: 'before Asia opens') forced Federal Council to commit in writing tonight (R4-R5), compressed legal review (R3: 'two-hour deadline'), drove hold-through timing (R8: '7am calls')
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: DECISIVE: fear of Monday panic drove Friday statement (Wealth Client R1: 'move money Monday at open'), hold-through mechanism (CS CEO R9: 'seventy percent holding through Monday'), and 30B ceiling (Federal Council R9: 'ration Monday morning')
